author: Jeremy Goldstein
title: Landon Donovan 'could not be happier' for USMNT hero with 'incredible story' - NewsBreak
text: Wednesday night was the Diego Luna show for the USMNT in St Louis: Mauricio Pochettino's side relied on two goals from the rising Real Salt Lake star to advance to the Gold Cup Final with a narrow 2-1 win over Guatemala. During the FOX postgame , former USMNT star Landon Donovan remarked on Luna's journey. “3 years ago, Diego Luna was playing in the USL for the El Paso Locomotives," he said. Today, he pushed his team to a Gold Cup Final. Incredible story, could not be happier for that young man." Since his retirement, Donovan hasn't always spoken kindly of the American players, evidenced by his impassioned rant about Christian Pulisic ahead of the tournament. His speaking highly of Luna, 21, shouldn't be taken lightly. READ MORE: Emma Raducanu sparked anger with Wimbledon outfit that flouted long-standing dress code READ MORE: Tiger Woods' son Charlie's 'I'm broke' claim as true net worth clear after trust fund revelation Luna, starting at left midfield in Pochettino's narrow 4-2-3-1 formation, scored in the fourth and the 15th minutes to secure the victory. The USMNT were mostly outplayed from that point forward. His first goal came from an opportunistic rebound, as he lifted a saved shot from goalkeeper Kenderson Navarro and into the Guatemalan net. The second game from a Malik Tillman switch. Luna did most of the work: taking on an opposing defender before silkily firing near post, echoing Harvey Elliott's recent solo-goal for England at the U21 European Championships. Luna was asked what was different about this USMNT performance from other ones. "The grit and determination, which we’ve been lacking, to be hones," he answered. "This is where we have to showcase it. There’s 90 minutes and we have to play for each one.” “It's an honor [to play for the USMNT], I am extremely grateful for the opportunity. Like a lot of other players here, this is the No. 1 dream for a player is to represent the program.” Donovan is right about Luna's rise. The US international began his career in the San Jose Earthquakes youth program before jumping ship for Barcelona's American academy in Arizona. READ MORE: Ex-USMNT star believes Mauricio Pochettino is taking role ‘personally’ after statement win READ MORE: Jets owner Woody Johnson faces major setback days after $254M Premier League investment Luna inked a professional contract with El Paso in 2021 to play in the USL, America's second division. Within a year, he set the USL transfer record at $250,000 and joined Real Salt Lake. He broke through with 16 goal involvements in 2024 to break into the USMNT. Ahead of the Gold Cup Final, he's up to 10 career international caps and three goals. The USMNT will play the winner of Mexico and Honduras in the Gold Cup Final.
